extracted.intended_audience: ICML 2025 Area Chairs (program committee Area Chairs)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and standards for Area Chairs at ICML 2025 on bidding, reviewer assignment and management, triaging ethical concerns, composing meta-reviews, and enforcing reviewing policies and timelines for assigned submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and meeting AC deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Please make sure you are available in the key reviewing periods, and are able to meet the AC deadlines (see key dates below).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize yourself with the bidding period, review deadlines, emergency reviewing period, author response/discussion windows, meta-review deadline, and AC-SAC discussion period; be responsive throughout the reviewing period, especially to assigned reviewers and your SAC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarity with instructions, reviewer guidance, and ethics/AI policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Please read the entirety of the area chair instructions (this document), the reviewer instructions, as well as the ethical conduct and use of generative AI policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read Reviewer Instructions and Publication Ethics pages; review Peer Reviewing memes for informal guidance; ensure you understand prohibitions (e.g., generative AI use) and reporting mechanisms for violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain up-to-date OpenReview profile and COI declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Please make sure your OpenReview profile is up-to-date, including conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate profile and COI information is used for assignments and conflict checking; check early and update if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding and indicating areas of expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate your areas of research expertise, and “bid” on submissions to meta-review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bids are done in OpenReview and help with assignment of submissions to ACs; bid during the bidding period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check meta-reviewing assignments and report problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Check your meta-reviewing assignments and notify your Senior Area Chair (SAC) of any problems (e.g., conflicts of interest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SAC is your first point of contact for issues; report conflicts or other assignment problems promptly so they can be resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure each submission has four qualified reviewers and manage assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that each assigned submission is assigned four qualified reviewers, and adjust assignments as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Modify Reviewer Assignments interface in OpenReview to add/unassign reviewers, sort by Affinity Score or bids for better matches, and avoid making more than two reviewer substitutions per submission without SAC approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not make more than two reviewer substitutions per submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer assignments will attempt to balance a number of concerns, so please do not make more than two reviewer substitutions per submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If additional substitutions are absolutely necessary, obtain approval from your SAC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure at least three high-quality, respectful reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that each assigned submission receives at least three high-quality reviews, each written in a respectful and professional manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check reviews as they come in; ask reviewers to revise (add justification, clarify points/questions, adjust tone/language) if needed; recruit emergency reviewers if reviewers miss deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruit emergency reviewers appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruit emergency reviewers as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First contact potential emergency reviewers via email to confirm willingness and communicate a meaningful deadline; then invite via OpenReview. Use the pool of available emergency reviewers, check 'Show reviewers with fewer than max assigned papers' to find eligible emergency reviewers; do not invite reviewers who have a full quota. If needed and as last resort, you may add yourself as a reviewer by asking your SAC to invite you (or, after the March 17 update, invite via AC console where allowed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to add reviewers not already in the reviewer pool
rubrics_metrics.description: You may ask your SAC to add a reviewer who is not currently in the reviewer pool. UPDATE: As of March 17, ACs are now able to do this by themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact potential reviewer personally first. In OpenReview, search all reviewers and if not found, type their email and click 'Invite Assignment'. Note COI checks may block or delay assignment if the reviewer must register for OpenReview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifying reviewer assignments in OpenReview
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions to un-assign, filter, sort, and add reviewers via the Area Chair Console's Modify Reviewer Assignments link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To un-assign click 'Trash' icon. Filter to show reviewers below quota with 'Only show reviewers with fewer than max assigned papers'. Sort by 'Affinity Score' rather than default 'Assignment' to surface most relevant reviewers. Use 'Assign' / 'Invite Assignment' to add reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit reviewer count and communicate prioritization when many reviews exist
rubrics_metrics.description: Try to not end up with too many (say, 5+) reviewers for any single submission, as this can be a burden to authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you end up with many reviews, inform authors and reviewers that authors cannot be expected to respond to all reviews; tell authors which reviews to prioritize and consider this when forming your meta-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitating reviewer discussions and enforcing protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage reviewers in discussions of submissions and encourage reviewers to discuss submissions with each other (and with you) by posting and responding to notes on OpenReview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the protocol of the Author-Reviewer discussions is followed by authors and reviewers. AC-reviewer discussions are not visible to authors; encourage reviewers to update their reviews after discussion. Make sure reviewers read authors' responses and acknowledge them by the stated deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response / author-reviewer discussion protocol compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: After the authors' responses are posted, make sure that your reviewers read them (and acknowledge that they have done so) by the stated deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the conference protocol which limits the number of rounds of communication between authors and reviewers; consult provided blog post/links for motivation and detailed instructions on handling the author response and discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compose informed meta-reviews and accept/reject recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully read the reviews and discussions to make accept/reject recommendations and compose informed meta-reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each meta-review should summarize the key points that justify your accept/reject recommendation (from reviews or anonymized discussions). Submit recommendations and meta-reviews for all submissions by the deadline; be prepared for your SAC to request clarifications or calibration after the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use review form item responses (not aggregate numeric scores) to inform recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: The review form this year is new and has specific items that reviewers are required to complete. Your recommendations and meta-reviews should be informed by the review form responses, as opposed to just relying on average (or other aggregate) numerical scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no numerical 'confidence' scores this year; instead use items like which aspects were checked and the reviewer's level of familiarity with prior literature to synthesize reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide ratings of the reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Please provide ratings of the reviewers for your assigned submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these ratings to highlight reviewers who go above-and-beyond and to identify those who are delinquent or shirk responsibilities; most reviewers are expected to 'meet expectations'. Ask your SAC for advice if unsure how to rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical conduct prohibitions (privileged information, collusion, Generative AI)
rubrics_metrics.description: ICML prohibits use of privileged information for any purpose other than reviewing, use of Generative AI tools in reviewing, and all forms of collusion (explicit or tacit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use submissions or review content with Generative AI; do not use privileged information outside reviewing; report suspected unethical conduct via the Ethics Violation Reporting form. Violations may lead to sanctions, rejection of the violator's submissions, and investigation by ICML's oversight committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict prohibition on use of Generative AI tools for reviewing/meta-reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Generative AI tools (such as LLMs) for reviewing is strictly prohibited. Reviewers cannot use Generative AI tools to write their reviews, and reviewers cannot input any content from any submission or review into a Generative AI tool. The same goes for ACs vis-à-vis meta-reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Publication Ethics page for detailed AI policy; do not paste confidential submission text into any LLM or other generative tool; violations are treated as ethical misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics triage categories and triage responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of the ethics review process, your job is to triage flags raised by reviewers by selecting one of the categories: No action necessary; AC involvement; Ethics review needed; Integrity review needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the illustrative category examples on the Publication Ethics page. 'No action necessary' applies when concerns are tenuous or not directly connected to the contribution. 'AC involvement' applies when reviewers/authors can remediate via discussion or added text. 'Ethics review needed' when you need external ethics reviewers. 'Integrity review needed' when program chairs must review issues like plagiarism or AI-generated papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review process and follow-up responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper is forwarded to ethics reviewers, expect two ethics reviews; ethics reviewers will provide feedback and, where possible, constructive remediation advice. If ethical issues are beyond remediation, an Ethics Chair may serve as a third reviewer and Program Chairs will decide on acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ethics reviewers indicate reasonable mitigations, ACs are responsible for working with authors to ensure these mitigations are enacted. Forward ethics flags promptly and provide the most relevant area of concern when escalating so the paper is routed to appropriate ethics reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling application-driven machine learning papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors could check a box to identify their submission as an 'application-driven machine learning paper'. See supplementary guidelines for how to handle these papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'application-driven' note will appear after the keywords; consult the referenced Reviewer Instructions page for supplementary handling guidance and any special considerations.
